question: Do high-fidelity CRISPR-Cas9 variants reduce genome-wide off-target editing?

starFinding.text: Yes: the high-fidelity variant SpCas9-HF1 reduces genome-wide off-target editing to undetectable levels for standard non-repetitive sequences while retaining on-target activity comparable to wild-type SpCas9 for over 85% of sgRNAs tested.
starFinding.sourceQuote: SpCas9-HF1 retains on-target activities comparable to wild-type SpCas9 with >85% of single-guide RNAs (sgRNAs) tested in human cells. Notably, with sgRNAs targeted to standard non-repetitive sequences, SpCas9-HF1 rendered all or nearly all off-target events undetectable by genome-wide break capture and targeted sequencing methods.

top3.text: The paired double-nicking strategy using a Cas9 nickase reduces off-target activity by 50- to 1,000-fold in cell lines without sacrificing on-target cleavage efficiency.
top3.sourceQuote: We demonstrate that paired nicking can be used to reduce off-target activity by 50–1,000 fold in cell lines and facilitate gene knockout in mouse zygotes without sacrificing on-target cleavage efficiency.

top3.text: The hyper-accurate variant HypaCas9 achieves dramatically improved genome-wide specificity over wild-type SpCas9 by GUIDE-seq, matching or exceeding SpCas9-HF1 and eSpCas9(1.1), without compromising on-target activity.
top3.sourceQuote: we design a new hyper-accurate Cas9 variant (HypaCas9) that demonstrates high genome-wide specificity without compromising on-target activity in human cells. Our GUIDE-seq analysis revealed that HypaCas9 exhibits dramatically improved genome-wide specificity compared to WT SpCas9, and shows equivalent or better genome-wide specificity relative to both SpCas9-HF1 and eSpCas9(1.1) for all sgRNAs examined.

doNotPromote: The Kulcsár et al. (2017) supporting quote — 'The propensity for off-target activity of Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 (SpCas9) has been considerably decreased by rationally engineered variants with increased fidelity (eSpCas9; SpCas9-HF1)' — must NOT be ranked #1: it is a background/introductory statement crediting prior variants (eSpCas9, SpCas9-HF1), not this paper's own novel result about HeFSpCas9.

The fCas9 result — 'Fusions of catalytically inactive Cas9 with FokI nuclease domain (fCas9) ... edits target DNA sites with >140-fold higher specificity than wild-type Cas9 and at least fourfold than that of paired nickases' — must NOT be #1: it is a narrower alternative-approach fold-specificity claim from a review, not the central genome-wide answer.

The HiFi Cas9 20-fold single-site INDEL reduction ('reduced INDEL frequency at the dominant off-target site by 20 fold') must NOT be #1: it is a single-locus figure, not a genome-wide summary of the effect.
